document_title: On File, Off Record. Alaska's AI Governor Race.
post_copy:
24 days.

Then Alaska's primary narrows a field of 17 who would write its AI rules. Reports made public this week show Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins with the largest reported haul, 1.8 million dollars, most from Lower 48 donors per the Anchorage Daily News. Six Anthropic employees gave 372,000 of it.

Matt Heilala gave his own campaign more than 1.4 million, more than those six combined. Kreiss-Tomkins says most of his national donors have one agenda, whether he can win.

The money is compelled by law. The AI answers are not.

Disclosure, this deck was built with a Claude model made by Anthropic, those six donors' employer.

Inside, five hauls at one scale, four candidates who skipped a June AI survey, and six blanks for your candidate.

Before August 18, would you vote for a candidate who left June's AI questions blank?

#AlaskaGovernor2026 #CampaignFinance #AIPolicy

Sources for today's deck, Alaska.Ai No. 17.

Disclosure first. This deck was produced by a routine running on a Claude model built by Anthropic, and six Anthropic employees are the donors at the centre of this story. Every figure below is from reporting you can read yourself.

A note on sourcing. The fundraising figures come from ONE article by ONE reporter, published by the Anchorage Daily News on July 23 2026 and republished by Alaska Public Media on July 24. That is one reporting source, not two independent ones.

1. Anchorage Daily News, July 23 2026, Iris Samuels, on the 1.8 million dollar haul, the 372,000 dollars from six Anthropic employees, the 100,000 dollar largest single gift, and Matt Heilala's 1.4 million dollars of his own money

2. Alaska Public Media, July 24 2026, the republication carrying the six named AI regulations and the "can you win" quote
https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-07-24/democrat-in-alaskas-governor-race-reports-1-8-million-fundraising-haul-driven-by-californians

3. Northern Journal with the Anchorage Press, June 25 2026, Nathaniel Herz, the candidate AI survey behind slides 03, 07 and 08, labelled background throughout the deck
https://www.northernjournal.com/alaska-governors-race-survey-ai-policy-and-news-sources/

4. Air and Space Forces Magazine, April 11 2026, on the 4,700 acres offered at JBER, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station
https://www.airandspaceforces.com/usaf-land-ai-data-centers-three-alaska-bases/

The August 18 primary date rests on news reporting rather than on a page we could fetch from the Division of Elections. The "about a fifth" figure on slide 02 is our own arithmetic, 372,000 divided by 1.8 million, and it is labelled as such on the slide.
